programme.title: Exploration Volcano
programme.desc: Chris Horsley specializes in volcano exploration.In the program, he brings documentarians from around the world to volcanic trails to show them the effects of eruptions, which can wreak havoc and threaten communities.Chris's great expedition spans a wide range - from the jungles of the Congo to the lava-burnt cities of the Canary Islands, from the distinctive glacial plains of Iceland to the smoking archipelagos of Italy.In each episode, his team must face unique and unpredictable terrain.However, the team does not stop at anything.He wants to complete each mission, whether it's collecting molten lava straight from the source or installing state-of-the-art volcano monitoring systems.These activities are necessary to better understand the functioning of ruthless natural giants.

programme.title: Spy in the Ocean
programme.desc: The creators of the four-episode series present the journey of specially constructed animal replicas equipped with cameras to the ocean.Their goal is to bring closer the deeply hidden life of creatures inhabiting this inaccessible and dynamic ecosystem.Using breakthrough technology, including:modern LCD screens, record surprising behaviors and relationships of sea animals.Viewers will see colorful coral reefs, rocky coastlines, Thai macaques fishing, unusual behavior of seals, socialization of sperm whales and a complicated ritual between hermit crabs.The over thirty spies include a sperm whale, a herring, a puffer, a hermit crab, a clownfish and a dolphin.The production took three years on four oceans of the world Filmmakers used new technologies to present the magic of the underwater world from a previously unavailable perspective.Robots equipped with cameras - confusingly similar to sea animals - set off on a spy mission.They not only passively recorded their surroundings, but also interacted with representatives of various species.The spectacular recordings were made into a documentary series that combines a fascinating narrative with impressive photos and humor.Its characters include sperm whales, octopuses, macaques, puffers, crabs and marlins.Underwater Geniuses One of the robotic spies took the form of a baby sperm whale.Not only cameras were installed there, but also hydrophones recording sounds.The three-meter-long baby was supposed to arouse the maternal instinct of the female it encountered.It greeted him with characteristic clicks.The moving meeting scene gave insight into the social intelligence of these giants.On an isolated Thai island, a dummy monkey spied on a diving flock of macaques.Cameras recorded their clever use of tools and carefree fun.In turn, the mechanical cephalopod went to meet the coconut octopus.Their interaction showed that true geniuses live in depths inaccessible to man.

programme.title: Dynasties II
programme.desc: The authors present the fate of wild animals that, living in often difficult conditions, persistently fight for the survival of their families.Each episode concerns a representative of a different species and members of its herd.Viewers will learn, among others:the story of the eight-year-old cheetah Kali, a resident of the grassy plains in western Zambia.Despite her relatively old age, the female desperately protects her family, teaching her daughters to be independent.A resident of Kenya, an inexperienced elephant, tries to secure the existence of her twins and unite the herd after the death of the leader.A puma from Patagonia takes care of four cubs alone.The program also features croquets, whose females are fighting an internal fight for dominance, as well as a young meerkat queen and Mac the macaque, trying to maintain his dominant role in the herd and father an offspring, thus initiating his own monkey dynasty.

programme.desc: The host of the program, Professor Brian Cox, presents selected information about the solar system.Viewers will learn about planets and moons covered with volcanoes that erupt with fire and ice.In the following parts, the scientist talks about the most interesting atmospheric conditions that were noticed on celestial bodies neighboring the Earth.He visits landscapes created by dust whirls, mountains covered with metallic frost and monsoon rains on one of the moons.In addition, Professor Cox will introduce viewers to frozen regions of the solar system, including a dwarf planet with mountains of solid ice floating on it, as well as a black and white moon.
